rows.claim: A tool failure must arrive inside the tools/call result with isError true so the calling agent can read it and branch; protocol-level errors are reserved for transport and discovery failures.
rows.quote: Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result object, with `isError` set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error response.
rows.steal: In any new MCP tool wrapper, raise on caller-fixable failure so mag/mcp_server.call_tool wraps it as isError; the pattern is implemented in mag/estate_bridge.py this lane and should be reused verbatim for R4's broker-gated tools.
rows.falsifier: A tool failure surfacing as a JSON-RPC error object (code/message) instead of a result carrying isError true.

rows.law: one tool per verb, estate_ prefix
rows.claim: Bridge tools are named estate_<verb>, one per verb; a generic run-tool proxy that takes a verb or tool name as an argument is forbidden.
rows.quote: Naming: `estate_` prefix, one tool per verb, never a generic "run tool" proxy.
rows.steal: When R4 adds estate_dirac_bank and broker authority, register them as separate static entries in tools/__init__.py TOOL_MAP and refuse any generic passthrough verb at gate review.
rows.falsifier: A bridge surface entry whose schema includes a tool-name or verb string it dispatches on.

rows.law: chain repair never crosses the bridge
rows.claim: Only dry verify is a bridge verb; real verkle-chain repair stays a seat-internal and operator verb because the blast radius is the estate's integrity spine.
rows.quote: Decision: chain_repair(real) is NOT exposed to external agents in v1. It stays a seat-internal + operator verb.
rows.steal: Keep estate_chain_repair permanently out of TOOL_MAP (asserted in tests/test_mcp_bridge_r1.py::test_never_exposed_repair_bank_and_control_words); a cloud agent needing repair files a finding and a funded seat executes.
rows.falsifier: estate_chain_repair, or any non-dry chain writer, appearing in tools/list on any profile.

rows.law: funded keys never cross the bridge
rows.claim: Driver status exposes heartbeat, off flag and work state only; work lanes and provider keys are unreachable by construction and are additionally scrubbed in code.
rows.quote: the lanes carry live provider keys, including the funded Nous key read from the hermes .env, and keys never cross the bridge;
rows.steal: Reuse mag/estate_bridge.py _redact on any future surface that serializes driver or lane state (dashboards, receipts); land the scrub next to the serializer, and keep the redaction test watching for nous-/sk- shaped strings.
rows.falsifier: A provider key value or key-named field surviving unredacted in a driver status response.

rows.claim: WaterGraph.to_spec serializes elev/kind/volume/steam but not a sill node's sill value while from_spec reads it, so a sill-gated graph round-trips through the bridge tick tool with its gate silently lost.
rows.steal: Water-graph owner: add "sill": v.sill to the node dict in to_spec (mag/water_graph.py:252) and extend the round-trip test; one line plus one assert, filed as observation 1 in watch/inbox/ball2/mcp-bridge-r1.md.
rows.falsifier: Round-trip a sill-gated graph through to_spec/from_spec and tick: identical gate behavior would kill this law.
